ANSWER — Interaction effect of BCG vaccination × prior medical history on COVID-19 severity:

In an ordinal (proportional-odds, cumulative-logit) logistic regression on the 148 infected subjects with a valid severity, controlling for patient interaction frequency (patients_seen), the BCG × prior-medical-history interaction odds ratio is **0.71 (95% CI 0.19–2.64, Wald p = 0.61)** — i.e., not statistically significant.

Interpretation: the BCG association with HIGHER severity is present among subjects WITHOUT prior medical history (OR 1.45) but is essentially null among those WITH prior medical history (OR 1.03). The interaction OR of 0.71 means the BCG effect on higher-severity odds is attenuated ~29% in the presence of prior medical history. (Reciprocal 1.41 is the same interaction on the "lower-or-equal severity" scale.)

The proportional-odds assumption is supported by the Brant score test (p=0.74); a naive LRT is borderline (p=0.016) but unreliable here because the non-PO alternative model is near-singular. Sensitivity (MH incl. free-text) gives OR 0.73 (p=0.66) — robust.
